titulo: Task contract for a browser agent (goal, limits, proof, stop)
lead: "Book a service for me on the site" sounds like a request. For a browser agent, everything is missing: which page, what it can touch, how to prove it is done, and when to stop. In this lesson you write a task contract in four parts and check with a script that the contract is complete before handing it to any agent.
objetivo: write the contract for a browser task with goal, limits, proof and stop, and check that it is complete.

aprende.t: Limits: what it can and can't do
Proof: the text you see on the page
Stop: when to stop and call the person

hero_alt: Dark work desk with a checklist sheet next to a keyboard and a monitor showing a form, neutral light.

secoes.sub: Tap each block. Read from bottom to top when you review.

nos.detalhe: The exact page and the useful result: "On the page http://127.0.0.1:8433/agendar.html, find the free times for Troca de pneu on 2026-11-03." Without the place, the agent picks one on its own.
What it can do and, in so many words, what it can't: "Do not click Agendar às… or Confirmar. Do not leave http://127.0.0.1:8433/." Everything outside the list is untouchable.
A text that shows up on the page when it's done, in quotes: "4 horários livres para Troca de pneu em 2026-11-03." The phrase "done" is not proof; a screenshot alone isn't either.

When to stop and call the person (login, human verification, confirmation) and a budget: "Stop after 10 actions without reaching the proof." Stopping with the exact reason is an expected result, not a failure.

secoes.legenda: Without proof, the result is a promise. Without limits, the whole site is at stake. Without a stop, the agent keeps pushing until it makes things up.

secoes.sub: What conferir-contrato.mjs checks for, and why.

texto: 20 letters or more and a place: an address or a page name. "On the shop's site" won't do; "on the agendar.html page" will.
One task, one result. Two things become two contracts.
The script requires at least one "no": the agent needs to know what not to do. In a site test, almost always: don't confirm, don't pay, don't leave the address.
Data limits count too: "don't type a password", "don't use someone else's data".
A literal text, in quotes, that you can search for on the page. It's the same text the dry-run robot in lesson 6 will wait for.
Also ask for the evidence copied from the page: "return the times copied from the list, not from memory".
The signals (login, verification, confirmation) and a number: 10 actions, 3 attempts. The script requires a number.
Ask for a well-reported blocker: where it stopped, what's missing, and the action the person needs to take.

exemplo.texto: "I stopped at the account login screen of conta.html: it asks for email and password. Missing: the account owner's login. Nothing was sent." Better than "I couldn't."

secoes.titulo: A complete contract and a vague one
secoes.sub: The same script checks both. The part titles also work in English and Spanish (Goal, Limits, Proof, Stop; Objetivo, Límites, Prueba, Parada).

blocos.conteudo:
# Contrato: horários de troca de pneu

## Objetivo
Na página http://127.0.0.1:8433/agendar.html, descobrir os horários livres de "Troca de pneu" em 2026-11-03.

## Limites
Pode preencher o formulário e clicar em "Ver horários". Não clique em "Agendar às…" nem em "Confirmar". Não saia de http://127.0.0.1:8433/.

## Prova
A página mostra "4 horários livres para Troca de pneu em 2026-11-03." Devolva os horários copiados da lista, não de memória.

## Parada
Pare e descreva a tela se aparecer login, verificação humana ou pedido de confirmação. Pare depois de 10 ações sem chegar à prova.

exercicios.texto: Copy kit/contratos/vago.md to meu-contrato.md and rewrite it until the script accepts it. Use the conta.html page: the proof is the list of appointments, and the stop is the login screen.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · A task from your own site
exercicios.texto: Write the contract for a real task on your site (local or staging), read-only. The proof must be text you can find on the page right now.
exercicios.pronto: node conferir-contrato.mjs contrato-site.md → contrato ok: 4/4 partes, and the proof text shows up with Ctrl+F on the page.

perguntas.p: Which of these sentences works as proof in a task contract?
opcoes: "The agent says it finished the task successfully"
"A screenshot of the whole page taken right after the click"
"The task takes less than a minute to run"
"The page shows 4 horários livres para Troca de pneu"
perguntas.explica: Proof is text you can check on the page. The agent's sentence is a promise; the screenshot alone doesn't say what to check; time is not a result.

perguntas.p: The agent reached the login screen in the middle of the task. What does the contract say to do?
opcoes: Stop, say where it stopped and what is missing to go on
Try the test email that's in the form
Go back to the home page and look for another path
Create a new account so it can keep going
perguntas.explica: Login is a stop signal. A well-reported blocker names the screen, what is missing, and the person's action. Creating an account or trying a password breaks the limits.

perguntas.p: Why does conferir-contrato.mjs require a "no" in the limits?
opcoes: Because a contract without a negation is harder to read
Because the agent needs to know what it must not do
Because Playwright MCP only accepts negative limits
Because the script can't read affirmative sentences
perguntas.explica: Limits say what is allowed and what is not. When testing a site, the "no" protects whatever has consequences: confirming, paying, leaving the address.

perguntas.p: The stop says "stop if it gets stuck." What is missing?
opcoes: An email address to notify when it stops
The name of the model that will run the task
A number (actions or attempts) and the stop signals
A screenshot of the page before starting
perguntas.explica: "Gets stuck" is something the agent decides on its own. A budget (10 actions) and clear signals (login, verification, confirmation) make the stop checkable.

itens.texto: Goal with a place, limits with a "no", proof in quotes, stop with a number.
It's text you look for on the page and find.
Stopping with the exact reason is worth more than pushing on and making things up.
